kind: guard-logic self-check — SYNTHETIC per-GPU VRAM values, NO GPU in the loop
not_a_witness_for: the sanctioned 8-rank GPU-node LOAD_READY + serve read-back (that remains the open #4952 definition-of-done; this proves only the pre-flight gate's arithmetic and messaging)
summary: tools/glm52_ep_witness.sh now reads each visible GPU's live free/total VRAM ONCE before the CUDA build + rank spawn and refuses with a single actionable message, instead of surfacing N opaque per-rank FitTooBig walls after spawn. The #4952 report ('needs 73.23 GiB, device has 71.41 GiB' on every rank) was an environmental stale-residency refusal misread as a code regression; the load plan is already rank-local / EP-aware (internal/ggufload.EstimateExpertParallelLoadMemoryPlan). This gate stops the next such run from being misfiled.

required_free_derivation.formula: internal/compute.RequiredFreeBytes(<per-rank plan total bytes>, headroom) — the exact inverse of BudgetAfterHeadroom, the single home of the load-time fit arithmetic, so the pre-flight threshold can never disagree with the in-process RefuseMemoryPlanIfTooBig gate
required_free_derivation.provenance: per-rank plan totals from experiments/glm-gpu-witness/glm52-ep-load-plan-witness-2026-06-30.json (weights) + the #4952 ~2.08 GiB KV @ --context-budget-tokens 4096

ranks_7.note: exceeds an ~79 GiB-usable 80 GiB-class sm_80 card — RANKS=7 needs a bigger card or >=8 ranks

scenarios.name: A stale-residency (reproduces #4952)
scenarios.verdict: EP_PREFLIGHT_REFUSE (8/8 short ~1.9 GiB) — likely stale residency

scenarios.name: C config-too-tight
scenarios.verdict: EP_PREFLIGHT_REFUSE (7/7 CARD TOO SMALL — need > card total) — raise RANKS / lower context

correction.what_was_wrong: FALSE WITNESS. As published on 2026-07-15 this file named two things under code_under_test — 'tools/glm52_ep_witness.sh (EP_PREFLIGHT gate)' and 'internal/compute.RequiredFreeBytes + TestRequiredFreeBytesIsExactFitBoundary' — and NEITHER existed anywhere in the tree. The script had no pre-flight block and compute had no RequiredFreeBytes; the string 'RequiredFreeBytes' appeared only in this file and in two scratch notes. The scenario table below was therefore never executed against any code: it was a design sketch published in the shape of a result.
correction.what_changed: The named code was written, so the witness is now true rather than the claim withdrawn: internal/compute/requiredfree.go (RequiredFreeBytes, the exact inverse of BudgetAfterHeadroom, defined against fitsWithinReportedMemory rather than restating the formula), internal/compute/requiredfree_test.go (TestRequiredFreeBytesIsExactFitBoundary), and the '# --- pre-flight per-GPU free-VRAM gate' block in tools/glm52_ep_witness.sh. The scenarios below were then RUN, for the first time, on 2026-08-05 — all six pass, reproducing the verdicts and the 77.1 / 85.6 GiB thresholds exactly as published.
correction.how_it_stays_true: tools/glm52_ep_preflight_test.go does four things. (1) It resolves every code_under_test entry to a real file and symbol, keying on the gate's SUBSTANCE — both refusal arms, both fail-open arms, the exit-93 line — not just the EP_PREFLIGHT_* names, which a logging stub would keep; and it requires those entries to still be DECLARED, so shrinking code_under_test fails instead of quietly switching the check off. (2) It pins the gate's PLAN_GIB table and headroom against compute.RequiredFreeBytes, asserting the gate can neither admit a run the load then refuses nor refuse a loadable one. (3) It runs tools/glm52_ep_preflight_selfcheck.sh. (4) Critically, it matches the threshold the gate actually PRINTED against RequiredFreeBytes — check (2) alone re-derives the number in Go and would not catch a wrong expression in the shell.
correction.mutation_evidence: The threshold assertions were verified load-bearing, not assumed: replacing the gate's plan/(1-headroom) with plan*(1+headroom) in a scratch copy turns 4 of the 6 scenarios red. The pre-strengthening assertions did NOT catch that mutation — 73.23*1.05 = 76.89 GiB sits between the stale-residency 75.2 GiB and the pristine 78.6 GiB, so every published verdict stayed correct while the arithmetic was wrong. That gap was found by an adversarial review of this change set and closed before it shipped.
correction.still_not_a_witness_for: unchanged — see not_a_witness_for above. Correcting this file does NOT advance #4952's definition-of-done, which still requires a sanctioned GPU node.
correction.provenance_arithmetic_note: required_free_derivation.provenance says the plan totals are the EP weight totals plus '~2.08 GiB' of KV. They are not, quite: glm52-ep-load-plan-witness-2026-06-30.json measures 71.11 GiB at 8 ranks and 79.21 GiB at 7, and the published 73.23 / 81.33 reconcile only at ~2.12 GiB of KV (73.23-71.11=2.12; 81.33-79.21=2.12). The plan totals themselves are consistent and are what the gate uses; it is the '~2.08' prose that is off by ~0.04 GiB. Left as written above so the original claim is still readable, and restated correctly in tools/glm52_ep_witness.sh.

reproduce: bash tools/glm52_ep_preflight_selfcheck.sh — extracts the '# --- pre-flight per-GPU free-VRAM gate' block from tools/glm52_ep_witness.sh, stubs log()/OUT/DONE/VIS/RANKS and a mock nvidia-smi that echoes 'free, total' MiB per '-i <idx>', and runs the scenarios above plus an unarmed-rank-count case (no GPU needed). Also driven from Go by TestGLM52EPPreflightSelfcheckScenariosPass.
fail_open: the gate never blocks a run when nvidia-smi is absent or returns no reading (non-NVIDIA / CI host), and is overridable via REQUIRE_FREE_GIB for any other RANKS/context/model.
